editorial:
Imagine being a lonely kid who just wants a friend, only to find one inside an old mirror. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a boy with mental struggles who starts talking to his own reflection, but this version of him is actually a mean demon. The vibe is super dark and creepy from the start, making you feel bad for the kid while also being scared of what he is about to do. It is a slow burn that builds up a lot of tension as the demon pushes the boy to do things that are totally wrong.

What really sticks with you is how gross and mean the kills are. The acting is solid, though the pacing feels a bit slow in the middle. If you love movies that make you squirm, you will dig this. However, if you hate seeing innocent people get hurt, stay away. For the best experience, you should definitely grab the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection so you can see all the gore in high detail. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to check it out for a night.
endingExplained: In the end, the demon totally wins. After the boy kills everyone he was supposed to love, he realizes he is completely alone. The mirror creature doesn't actually care about him; it just wanted to cause pain. The movie wraps up with the boy trapped in a cycle of violence, showing that the demon has full control over his mind and life. There is no happy rescue, just a dark and sad finish.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves extreme horror and twisted stories.
